### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via searchAll (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `35faf20e10e6987737946b58ce2756e3bc0610b4` — the merge of head `a8fe932ef92d227f881c051a17a3916e2abf0545` into base `8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 35faf20e10e6987737946b58ce2756e3bc0610b4 && git checkout 35faf20e10e6987737946b58ce2756e3bc0610b4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e a8fe932ef92d227f881c051a17a3916e2abf0545 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e && git merge --no-ff a8fe932ef92d227f881c051a17a3916e2abf0545

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a8fe932ef92d227f881c051a17a3916e2abf0545`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.search-title-namefield.test.ts, content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx, .changeset/24087-search-title-namefield-first.md

Scope note: the schema face is `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` (the one `hits` path). Widened to every other path of the diff plus the cited `display-name.ts`, each read in the cited code at the head; no path is left as a TIER_DEFAULT remainder. Net diff read as merge-base `b0fe9fad` → head (5 files, +153/−38; the three-dot diff against `origin/main` `b1845ed6` is byte-identical, and `main` has not moved under any of the five files or `display-name.ts` since the merge-base).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Schema shape, exports, accept sets — nothing moves. RIGHT.** The only change in `protocol.zod.ts` is the string literal inside `SearchAllHitSchema.title`'s `.describe()` (lines 2572–2577 at the head). No key added, removed, renamed or retyped; no optionality change; no export touched. Consistent with the file list: no `api-surface/`, `authorable-surface/` or `json-schema.manifest/` shard moves, and `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:docs` all sit inside the green `TypeScript Type Check` job. The generated `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` rows (two occurrences of the hit table) are byte-equal to the new describe. The old sentence survives nowhere at the head (`git grep` of its distinctive fragment: zero hits).

2. **The describe text is TRUE of the code at this head, word for word. RIGHT.** Describe: "resolved in order: the declared primary-title pointer (`nameField`, ADR-0079; deprecated alias `displayNameField` still honored) → the object's deprecated `titleFormat` template → conventional name fields → first/last name → the record ID as a string." `renderTitle` at `protocol.ts:15589–15614`: (a) `titlePointer = obj.nameField ?? obj.displayNameField`, returned when the field exists on the object and the row's value is non-empty after trim; (b) `titleFormatSource` rendered with `{field}` / `{{field}}` placeholders; (c) `['name','full_name','title','subject','label','company'].filter(hasField)`; (d) `first_name` / `last_name`; (e) `String(row.id)`. Five steps, same order, same vocabulary. The alias is consulted only when `nameField` is absent (the `??`), which is what "deprecated alias still honored" meant before this PR too.

3. **The runtime reorder in `protocol.ts` is the card's Done-when arm 1 and nothing else. RIGHT.** The pointer moved out of the conventional candidate list to a first step with the same empty-falls-through semantic (`v != null && String(v).trim()`) and the same `hasField` guard; the conventional list is unchanged; the `.filter` lost its type predicate only because the list is now all string literals. The replaced test `titleFormat still outranks the pointer` was a #8786 scope-preservation pin asserting the old order, not a ruling; the card records no ruling for a deviation, so arm 1 binds as written. Pre-existing and untouched by this PR (noted, not a finding against it): a partially-resolved template still returns at `protocol.ts:15603` although the comment above says unresolved placeholders fall through; same before and after.

4. **Pins. RIGHT, with the real-engine caveat accepted.** Four new tests in the `[#24087]` block, every fixture passed through the real `provisionPrimary(…, { synthesize: false })` from `@objectstack/spec/data` (a declared subpath export; the test file is inside the package's `tsc --noEmit` program via `include: ["src/**/*"]`, so the green type check covers the fixture typing). THE PIN reproduces the card's measured shape (`titleFormat: '{process_name} · {record_id}'` beside `nameField: 'display_title'` text formula) and names the defect's signature negatively; two controls keep the template reachable (no title-eligible field ⇒ no stamp ⇒ `Order 42`; empty pointer value ⇒ template, not id); the fourth pins the H1 consequence. The dev's single ablation (template-first restored via the pointer guard) failed exactly the two predicted pins. The double is the file's existing boundary stand-in, not ObjectQL: `metadata-protocol` cannot import `@objectstack/objectql` (cycle, stated at `protocol.ts:15634–15639`), and the registry step that decides this behaviour — the stamp — is the real one. The real-engine palette pin's natural home (`packages/objectql/src/global-search-palette-recall.test.ts`) is correctly recorded as a carrier-less acceptance note.

5. **Census (Done-when 3). RIGHT for this repository.** At the head, outside tests, `*.object.ts`, `packages/spec`, `packages/lint` and `packages/cli`, the only runtime site that renders `titleFormat` is `searchAll` (`protocol.ts:15575`); `metadata-core/object-schema-fls-references.ts:743` rewrites the template's field references for FLS and titles nothing; `objectql`'s `resolveRecordTitle` / `resolveDisplayField` never read the key (`display-name.ts:220–225`). The objectui display-name chain is named as a lead, not a reading — correct, objectui was outside this session.

6. **Check-runs on the head, read live at 2026-10-17T17:56Z (40 runs).** Required contexts: `Lint & Repo Gates` success · `TypeScript Type Check` success · `Build Core` success · `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success · `Test Core` shards 1/6, 2/6, 5/6, 6/6 success, **`Test Core (3/6)` in_progress, `Test Core (4/6)` in_progress**. Every other completed run is success or an expected skip (`Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Packed-tarball smoke`, the matrix placeholder); `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, all three claim-branch checks: success. No failure, cancellation or timeout on the head. The two in-progress shards are the one reading this record could not close; the seat re-reads CI before any landing step, and a red on either shard voids this PASS for that head.

7. **Governed surfaces: none in the file list** (no `.claude/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/workflows/**`). Head repo equals base repo (not a fork). Draft, `Fixes #24087`, 191 changed lines, labels `documentation` / `size/m` / `tests` / `tooling`, no `skip-changeset`.

### ② Semver level

**RIGHT: `patch` × 2, and the `Clause-②` line reads `no` with no arm on both carriers.** The changeset `.changeset/24087-search-title-namefield-first.md` declares `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch` (a reader in a released package now obeys the precedence the contract already declared — a bug fix, so `patch`, never none and never `skip-changeset`) and `@objectstack/spec: patch` (the describe text ships in the tarball and the generated reference; no shape change). The PR body's third line and the changeset body both carry the declaration reading `no`: no accept set is widened (nothing new parses) and none is narrowed (nothing that parsed is refused), so no `(narrowing)` arm, no BREAKING, no ADR-0087 disposition marker owed; `Check Changeset` is green. The body goes beyond what a `patch` strictly owes by stating the visible consequence and ADR-0079 D3's migration (a text formula designated as `nameField`), which is the right text for an upgrading agent to grep.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every `deviations` entry and the one `open_questions` entry of os-dev-report 6237615038, answered:

1. **File-surface breach — `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` + the generated mdx. Accepted; it is why this review exists.** The claim fenced out `packages/spec` naming `resolveDisplayField` and the `titleFormat` describe, both untouched. The `SearchAllHitSchema.title` describe is the published contract of the very reader this PR changes, and the reorder made its sentence false. os-dev's rule 3 states the obligation in one line ("本轮改动令其变假或触碰的已发布缺陷必修"), and AGENTS.md's route rule 4 ("machine-readable surfaces must not lie") agrees. The breach is describe text only, declared in the PR body and the report, and it put the PR on the schema face at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER — this record is that review. Owed by the seat, not the dev: the in-place fix's second half under os-dev rule 3 — supplement the claim's declared file surface with `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` and `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` in the same round.

2. **Pin not over a real ObjectQL engine. Accepted** — package cycle verified in the cited code; the real `provisionPrimary` is applied to every fixture; the real-engine home is named with `carrier: none`. Not escalated.

3. **Worktree created from a pre-existing local branch at `b0fe9fad` = merge-base.** No effect on the diff (base identical; empty branch pushed before any edit). Accepted.

4. **`@objectstack/spec`'s own `pnpm test` not run locally; `test:repo` not run.** Describe-only spec change, no remaining copy of the old sentence at the head, spec build + `check:generated` reported green by the dev and confirmed by the `TypeScript Type Check` job. CI's `Test Core` is the gate — four shards green, two in progress as listed in ① item 6. Accepted on that reading.

5. **PR-body footer in the os-dev session-URL form; 6. zero label writes (changeset present, so `skip-changeset` rightly not applied); 7. platform PR auto-subscription declined.** All consistent with the dispatch contract. Accepted.

8. **H1 (`open_questions[0]`): a provisioned (stamped) `nameField` now outranks `titleFormat`, not only an authored one. Answer: A — accept as landed. Not escalated.** Grounds, read in the cited code: ADR-0079 D1 (a title is a real stored field, "not a template"), D4 (one resolution order for every consumer, `nameField ?? displayNameField ?? derivation`, which never contains `titleFormat`), D7 (the registry's designate-only stamp at `objectql/src/registry.ts:3522` inside `materializeBaseLayer`, called from `registerObject`, exists so the pointer "is reliably populated"); and `ObjectTitleCompleteness.status`'s docblock (`display-name.ts:326–355`): authorship is deliberately not recoverable after the stamp, so option B would need a new provenance surface built to keep a deprecated key alive, against the direction D3 sets. The dispatch's "measured first" item anticipated exactly this and directed mirroring `resolveDisplayField`; the card's arm 1 says the same. **Measured reach at the head, first-party metadata:** 65 `*.object.ts` files declare `titleFormat`; 60 also declare `nameField` (those are the card's arm 1, titled by the authored pointer — not H1); 5 are `titleFormat`-only. Of the five, `sys_audience_binding_suggestion` and `sys_share_link` are `enable.searchable: false` and never reach the palette; three do and change palette title from the template to the stamped field: `sys_attachment` → `file_name` (affix tier), `sys_notification_template` → `subject` (exact tier), `sys_record_share` → `object_name` (its `apiMethods: ['get','list']` whitelist serves `search` through `list` per `api-derivation.ts:145`). The changeset discloses this class and the migration; lint already warns `title-format-retired`. For the seat, not a blocker: those three first-party objects are the one place H1 thins a palette title (`sys_record_share` titled by its object name alone) — fold them into the family closing card the dispatch already plans for `titleFormat` readers, as a migration to an explicit `nameField` (text formula), rather than opening a reader-specific exception.

9. **`out_of_scope_findings`.** The objectui display-name chain (calendar/kanban card title, record H1 reading `titleFormat` first, per `spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` docblocks and the liveness ledger's `titleFormat: live` row) is the remaining family; correctly left unmeasured here and handed to the seat for one closing card after confirming at the pinned `.objectui-sha`. The second item is Acceptance-notes material and is recorded as such.

10. **Acceptance-note accuracy, minor:** the PR body says "roughly 30 other `*.object.ts` files declaring `titleFormat`"; the head count is 65 (60 with a `nameField` beside it). Not load-bearing for the verdict; the changeset's statement of reach is correct in kind.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24087-search-title-namefield-first`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JtSQQ3EWsbNPzyYMug1tXy`

**VERDICT: PASS**
